speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and tell me exactly when it first appeared relative to your fever and cold symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on her face look like slapped cheeks, and have you noticed any ring-like or lacy patterns on the rash on her trunk and extremities? Also, has she been in contact with anyone who had a similar rash recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, preceded by mild constitutional symptoms, is classic for Erythema Infectiosum.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Fifth disease (Erythema Infectiosum)
